evidence.curator_note: Equation 8.20, DISFAVORED branch (b): the reaction arrow leading FROM the 2-phenylethanol molecular ion TO this branch is drawn CROSSED OUT (a large X over the arrow next to the label '(b)'). This four-membered transition state (ring atoms O2-C1-C3 plus the migrating H8) would transfer the O-H hydrogen H8 directly to the BENZYLIC carbon C3 and cleave C1-C3, giving the MORE-STABLE toluene radical cation (C7H8+., m/z 92) plus neutral formaldehyde. The book rejects it: four- and three-membered transition-state rings are disfavored (text, same page), so despite the greater product stability the path does not compete with branch (a). Encoded with support_type=contradicted and peak status=rejected. ARC COUNT (convention D): the page draws a four-pointed 'bowtie'/star of roughly four fishhook (half-arrow) arcs inside the small four-membered TS (the O-H bond -> new C3-H bond, and the C1-C3 sigma -> C1=O2 carbonyl). Book draws ~4 fishhook arc(s); none is an implicit hook (4 single-electron fishhooks = the 2 encoded double-barbed 2e moves paired up). ENCODING: move<1> O2-H8 sigma -> new C3-H8 bond (H8 to the benzylic carbon, making the ring methyl of toluene); move<2> the C1-C3 sigma -> the new C1=O2 carbonyl pi (expelling neutral formaldehyde). CONVENTION C: the aromatic ring is NOT involved in this branch and rides through UNCHANGED; the delocalized ring radical cation is localized in ONE Kekule/distonic form (odd electron on C9, formal + on C10) consistently in precursor and product, so +. is a spectator. CONVENTION F: no m/z or % printed; observed_mz 92.0621 is the curator-computed monoisotopic m/z of C7H8+., status 'rejected', detected=false, relative_intensity omitted.
No MØD rule is indexed to equation 8.20 (rule_index by_equation has no '8.20' key). Consistent with the book crossing this branch out, there is nothing to cross-link.
